title: Round-2 extensions: PDE discovery (with traveling-wave degeneracy archived), control loop synthesized from the discovered model, and an evidence-chain gate
domain: equation discovery / PDEs / control systems / evaluation methodology
problem: (a) Does sparse discovery extend to PDEs from snapshot data, and when does support recovery fail? (b) Are discovered ODE models actionable -- can a controller built ONLY from the discovered model match one built from ground truth? (c) Can the report's numbers be mechanically verified against committed artifacts?
hypothesis: (a) Burgers and KdV are recovered from periodic-domain snapshots with held-out new-IC rollouts <5%; a single traveling wave makes support unidentifiable (P9). (b) A feedback-linearization PD controller from a polynomial (mismatched) discovered f_hat matches the oracle controller within IAE ratio <1.25 in the bounded-angle regime. (c) All headline numbers are checkable by script.
baseline: PDE-FIND (Rudy et al., Science 2017) for method; oracle-model controller for exp11; gplearn for GP comparison.
proposed_improvement: No method novelty claimed. Contributions: documented traveling-wave degeneracy with the failed first attempt preserved as evidence; sign-discipline lesson for derivative stencils (unit-tested); demonstration that discovered dynamics close the loop at oracle performance under known library mismatch; check_claims.py gate (35/35).
